entry.text: In 1791, authorities in France suppressed Justine or the Misfortunes of Virtue. In March 1801 the stocks of The New Justine and Juliette were seized when Sade was arrested at his publisher's office. The Cour Royale de Paris ordered the book's destruction on 19 May 1815.

entry.text: The Decameron was among the works burned in Florence in 1497 in a bonfire incited by Girolamo Savonarola. It was placed on the Index of 1559 under the instructions of Paul IV, and its prohibition was confirmed in the Index of 1564. In 1573 Pope Gregory XIII commissioned a revised edition in which the clergymen were replaced with secular people.

entry.text: The Chinese government banned Zhuan Falun and other publications on 24 July 1996. On 26 July 1999 the Ministry of Public Security called for the confiscation and destruction of all publications related to Falun Gong. By 30 July, Xinhua had reported confiscations of over one million Falun Gong books and other materials.
